baselineChecks.description: r1 reaches r2 on the r1-r2 link
r3 reaches r2 on the r2-r3 link

scenario: Three routers r1, r2 and r3 sit in a line: r1 - r2 - r3. The links are addressed and up and each router has a loopback, but no routing protocol runs. Each router reaches only its neighbours. The team wants loopbacks learned from a routing protocol, not static routes, and then wants the two ends of the line to reach each other.

checks.description: r1 has the r2-r3 link subnet learned by OSPF
r3 has the r1-r2 link subnet learned by OSPF

commonMistakes.mistake: Putting a router or an interface in a different area number
commonMistakes.recognise: show ospf neighbor is empty or the far subnet is missing from show route protocol ospf
commonMistakes.symptom: No route from OSPF for the far link subnet appears

doneWhen: r1 has a route to <private-address>/30 with protocol OSPF.
r3 has a route to <private-address>/30 with protocol OSPF.
The link interfaces are still up.
explanation: OSPF adjacencies form over the link interfaces in area 0.0.0.0, so each router floods its link subnets.
The route-exists checks show the far link subnet with protocol OSPF and a next hop through r2, so the protocol installed it.
stages.goal: Make r1, r2 and r3 exchange routing information over their point-to-point links in a single OSPF area, so that each end router learns the far link subnet from the protocol.
stages.hint: Look at which routes r1 and r3 hold for the far link subnet and by which protocol they were installed.

r1: set protocols ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface ge-0/0/0.0 interface-type p2p
r2: set protocols ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface ge-0/0/0.0 interface-type p2p
set protocols ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface ge-0/0/1.0 interface-type p2p
r3: set protocols ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface ge-0/0/0.0 interface-type p2p

stages.title: Bring up the routing area

checks.description: r1 learns r2's loopback by OSPF
r1 learns r3's loopback by OSPF
r3 learns r1's loopback by OSPF

commonMistakes.mistake: Loopback left out of the area on one router
commonMistakes.recognise: show route protocol ospf lacks the /32; ping reports no route to host
commonMistakes.symptom: That router's /32 is missing elsewhere, and the ping to it fails with no route

doneWhen: r1 and r3 each hold an OSPF route to the other end's loopback, and r1 also holds one to r2's loopback.
r1 can ping <private-address> and r3 can ping <private-address> with no loss.
The link interfaces are still up.
explanation: Once each loopback is in area 0.0.0.0 its /32 is flooded to every router and appears with protocol OSPF.
The ping succeeds because r1 has a route to r3's loopback via r2 and r3 has a return route to the r1-r2 link subnet from stage 1.
stages.goal: Make every router's loopback part of the routing area so the two ends of the line reach each other loopback to loopback across r2.
stages.hint: A loopback is not advertised until it is part of the protocol; it needs no neighbours.

r1: set protocols ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface lo0.0 passive
r2: set protocols ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface lo0.0 passive
r3: set protocols ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface lo0.0 passive

stages.title: Prove end-to-end reachability

r1: set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address <private-address>/30
set interfaces lo0 unit 0 family inet address <private-address>/32
r2: set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address <private-address>/30
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address <private-address>/30
set interfaces lo0 unit 0 family inet address <private-address>/32
r3: set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address <private-address>/30
set interfaces lo0 unit 0 family inet address <private-address>/32

startState.description: Every link interface and loopback is addressed and up; no routing protocol is configured on any router. Each router reaches only its directly connected neighbours.

summary: Three routers in a line are brought into one OSPF area so that every loopback is learned by the protocol and the two ends reach each other.
title: Bring a Three-Router Core onto a Single Link-State Area

nodes.role: the middle router the path crosses
the other end of the line
